profile.name: Chuvash folk dance
profile.insight: The Chuvash State Academic Song and Dance Ensemble, founded in 1924, preserved and performed Chuvash folk dances even during World War II at the front lines.
profile.profile: Chuvash folk dance features round wedding dances with hand clapping and foot stamping, performed traditionally by the Chuvash people of Russia. The dance is preserved and showcased by the Chuvash State Academic Song and Dance Ensemble, which originated as the Chuvash National Choir in 1924. The ensemble combines music and dance to represent the cultural heritage of Chuvashia across Russia.
profile.profile_long: Chuvash folk dance is a traditional dance form of the Chuvash people, an ethnic group in Russia. It is characterized by round dances often performed at weddings, incorporating hand clapping and foot stamping, known locally as “tasha.” These dances are communal and celebratory, reflecting social and cultural rituals of the Chuvash community. The preservation and public performance of these dances have been championed by the Chuvash State Academic Song and Dance Ensemble, originally founded in 1924 as the Chuvash National Choir by composers F.P. Pavlov and V.P. Vorobyov. This ensemble gathered and processed Chuvash folk songs and dances, touring major Russian cities such as Moscow and Leningrad in the 1920s. In 1939, the choir was renamed to include dance explicitly, under the direction of composer A.G. Orlov-Shuzm, who led the ensemble in presenting the music and dance of the peoples of the Russian Soviet Federative Socialist Republic (RSFSR). Despite the turmoil of World War II, the ensemble continued its activity, performing at the Bryansk and Kalinin Fronts in 1943, demonstrating the cultural resilience of the Chuvash people. The ensemble has received multiple honors, including the title of academic ensemble in 1994 and the State K. Ivanov's Prize of the Chuvash Republic, underscoring its importance in maintaining Chuvash cultural traditions. The dance itself, while not described in technical detail in the sources, is closely linked to the ensemble’s performances, which combine music, song, and dance to represent Chuvash identity. The ensemble’s work ensures that the Chuvash folk dance remains a living tradition, performed publicly and preserved for future generations.

sections.origins_and_history: The Chuvash folk dance tradition is rooted in the cultural practices of the Chuvash people of Russia. The Chuvash State Academic Song and Dance Ensemble, founded in 1924 as the Chuvash National Choir by F.P. Pavlov and V.P. Vorobyov, played a key role in collecting, processing, and performing Chuvash folk songs and dances. The ensemble toured major Russian cities in the 1920s, spreading awareness of Chuvash culture. In 1939, it was renamed to include dance explicitly, and under the leadership of A.G. Orlov-Shuzm, it performed music and dance of the RSFSR peoples. The ensemble remained active during World War II, performing at front lines in 1943. It has since received multiple honors, including the title of academic ensemble in 1994.
sections.how_it_is_danced: The dance is described as round wedding dances featuring hand clapping and foot stamping, known as “tasha.” Specific technique, footwork, rhythm, or formation details are not described in the sources.
sections.music_and_instruments: The ensemble performs Chuvash folk songs and dances, but specific musical instruments or vocal styles used in the dance are not detailed in the sources.
sections.costume_and_setting: Costume and setting details for Chuvash folk dance are not described in the sources.
sections.occasions_and_meaning: Chuvash folk dances are traditionally performed at weddings and communal celebrations, serving as expressions of cultural identity and social cohesion within the Chuvash community.
sections.notable_figures: F.P. Pavlov and V.P. Vorobyov founded the original Chuvash National Choir in 1924. A.G. Orlov-Shuzm was the first artistic director after the choir became the Song and Dance Ensemble in 1939. Later conductor Kazatchkov S.A. also led the ensemble.
sections.regional_variants: No regional variants of Chuvash folk dance are described in the sources.
sections.lineage: Chuvash folk dance is part of the broader folk traditions of the Chuvash people in Russia, preserved and promoted by the Chuvash State Academic Song and Dance Ensemble since the early 20th century.
